summary: Iteration 28 — four items: cost freeze, quotations removed, currency grouping, import template. Backend 17/17 pytest pass after fixing a REAL blocker in server.py:create_sale (NameError: 'was' undefined — crashed every POST /api/sales with 500). Cost freeze end-to-end verified: PUT an item cost 1.3× raises the item's current cost but leaves the item's /api/items/{id} profit, /api/reports/pnl year COGS+gross_profit AND the /api/reports/products row profit identical to the pre-change figures (±1 NGN rounding). A new quick sale after the bump stamps cost_at_sale = new_cost on the sale's line, confirming freeze cuts in at the moment of sale (verified via GET /api/sales/{id}). Quotations removal fully verified: GET/POST /api/quotes, GET /api/quotes/{id}, POST /api/quotes/{id}/convert all 404, GET /api/shortcuts no longer contains any 'quote' key, /invoices still 200. UI: /quotes, /quotes/new both render the Unmatched Route screen, /more does NOT contain testID more-quotes and the word 'Quotations' is not on the screen, the + sheet (fab-sheet) contains 'New invoice' and does NOT mention 'quotation' or 'New quote'. Import template verified: GET /api/import/template?target=customers returns columns=[name,phone,email,address,opening_balance] + csv + tredi_customers_template.csv filename; target=items returns [name,category,unit,cost_price,selling_price,quantity,barcode,photo_url]; both templates round-trip through POST /api/import/preview as 1 ready / 0 issues (round-trip proof). UI /settings/import exposes import-template-card, import-template button, lists the customers columns by default, and switching the Seg to 'Stock items' flips the listed columns to the items set. Regression: /api/invoices/{id} 200, /api/subscription 200 with plan=pro. Currency grouping — HOWEVER — only works on screens that use the shared Field with keyboardType='decimal-pad' (/stock/new qty/cost/selling and /customers/new opening are confirmed grouping — typing 1500000 shows 1,500,000 and 1234.56 shows 1,234.56). It does NOT work on /expenses/new (amount), /payments/new (amount) and /quick-sale (tendered) — these screens render raw <TextInput> directly, bypassing Field — and also does NOT work on /purchases/new (unit cost / qty / paid) because those Fields are passed keyboardType='numeric' (not 'decimal-pad'), which the Field.grouped guard reads strictly as a check for exactly 'decimal-pad'. The user complaint 'currency format not corrected' is therefore only half-fixed. Cleanup clean: TEST_iter28 item, customer and expense were created and deleted inside each test; one TEST_iter28 sale was created and cancelled; item cost restored to original. No deprecated packages, no SafeAreaView issues, no red-screens, no new RN warnings beyond the known Image.style.resizeMode deprecation already called out in iter27.

critical.issue: 500 Internal Server Error on EVERY quick sale — server.py create_sale referenced `was` dict that was never defined (leftover from the update_sale pattern). I fixed it by removing the dangling `if l.get('item_id') in was` block; stamp_costs already handles the None-cost-at-sale case correctly for a brand-new sale. Confirmed with a successful POST /api/sales + GET /api/sales/{id} with the new cost stamped on the line.

ui_bugs.issue: Thousands separator does not kick in. The amount input is a raw <TextInput testID=expense-amount keyboardType=decimal-pad .../> inside the big amount box (expenses/new.tsx:103), not the shared <Field>, so Field.grouped never runs. Typing 1500000 reads '1500000' and 1234.56 reads '1234.56'. Fix: either swap this one input for <Field> or hoist the group() formatting into a tiny wrapper around TextInput that respects keyboardType.
Same shape as expenses/new — raw <TextInput testID=payment-amount keyboardType=decimal-pad .../> at payments/new.tsx:108, no grouping. Typing 1500000 stays '1500000'.
Same shape — raw <TextInput testID=tender-input keyboardType=decimal-pad .../> at quick-sale.tsx:224, no grouping. The quick sale cash tendered box is one of the most money-heavy inputs in the app.

Uses <Field> but passes keyboardType='numeric' (purchases/new.tsx:163, 239, 240). The Field.grouped check is strictly `rest.keyboardType === 'decimal-pad'`, so numeric does not qualify. Either (a) change these three Fields to decimal-pad (unit cost and 'paid' are money, qty is a count — decimal-pad is still right because the user may want decimals on bulk packs), or (b) extend Field.grouped to include 'numeric'.

action_items: Finish ITEM 3: wire the shared Field (or an equivalent group() wrapper) into the four raw/'numeric' money inputs — /expenses/new amount, /payments/new amount, /quick-sale tendered, and /purchases/new unit cost/qty/paid — so the user sees commas while typing on every money box. Keep parseNum on save so the server still receives plain digits (already proven on /stock/new which saves 1500000 as 1500000 in Mongo).
No further backend work required for ITEM 1, 2 or 4 — all three are complete end-to-end. The create_sale 500 bug is fixed in this iteration (server.py 854–857) and verified by pytest.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:854 (before fix): `if l.get('item_id') in was:` referenced an undefined local — classic copy-paste from update_sale's `was = {...}` map. Any POST /api/sales (offline sync as well, since sync() calls similar paths) that reached this branch returned 500. Fix applied: deleted the two-line block so stamp_costs is the single source of cost_at_sale on a new sale. Create-sale is now covered by test_new_sale_stamps_new_cost which proves the stamp.

deps.py stamp_costs + line_cost (cost freeze): correct — stamp_costs skips lines that already carry cost_at_sale (so re-applies on edits never clobber the original) and only reads the item's current cost for brand-new lines; line_cost falls back to the item's current cost only when there is no stamp (pre-migration rows). The year COGS / gross_profit figures held steady under a 1.3× cost bump as expected (verified by test_cost_change_does_not_move_history).

routes/offline.py import_template is a tiny GET and does the right thing — the sample row round-trips through import_preview with 1 ready, 0 issues on both targets, so the template csv and the importer are proven in lock-step. Note: the seeded demo customer 'Grace Mwangi' uses the exact phone the customers template suggests as the example row, so a user who downloads and uploads the template unchanged will see a 'duplicate · merge?' flag on the customer side — purely cosmetic, but worth either changing the sample phone or de-duping on name+phone exactly.

frontend/src/components/ui.tsx Field.grouped: `!nogroup && rest.keyboardType === 'decimal-pad'` is strict. On web keyboardType is mapped to inputMode='decimal'; the check reads the prop before the mapping, which is fine, but 'numeric' and 'number-pad' slip through. Consider widening to `['decimal-pad','numeric','number-pad'].includes(rest.keyboardType)` so the four screens above also pick up grouping without edits in the callers.

frontend/app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx ACTIONS list and frontend/app/(tabs)/more.tsx entries have no quotes shortcut. Backend routes/invoicing.py no longer registers /quotes handlers and shortcuts.py excludes the quote key. Quotations are consistently off everywhere I could reach them.

rca_of_issue: ITEM 1 (cost freeze) and the create_sale 500: when E1 added the stamp_costs flow in iter27-28, they lifted the `was = {old cost_at_sale per item}` idiom from update_sale into create_sale without noticing that a brand-new sale has nothing to carry over — the `was` symbol never existed in create_sale's local scope. Every POST /api/sales (even an empty 1-line one from the quick-sale screen) hit `l.get('item_id') in was` and raised NameError, which FastAPI returns as 500. The fix is one line: delete the carry-over block. stamp_costs alone handles both cases correctly: lines with an existing cost_at_sale (which only ever happens from offline sync replays) are kept, lines without one are stamped from the item's current cost. Confirmed by test_new_sale_stamps_new_cost — the stamp exactly matches the post-bump cost, meaning the freeze only affects FUTURE sales, which is what the owner asked for. ITEM 3 (currency grouping): the engineering intent in iter27 was to let Field do the formatting work globally; the implementation only touched Field, but four of the money screens use <TextInput> directly or pass keyboardType='numeric'. The group() helper is correct and the Field path is correct — it just isn't on every money screen yet.
